rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause, relocation assistance, buyouts, retaliation)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not end a covered tenancy without an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the notice. For no-fault terminations the landlord must pay or waive 2 months' rent as relocation assistance (3 months if the tenant is 62+ or disabled), give 30/60 days' notice, and offer re-rental if the unit is re-offered within 5 years. Buyouts are regulated and retaliation is prohibited.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months if senior/disabled) for no-fault terminations
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause
rules.effective_date_note: Division as expanded by O-21647 N.S., effective 2023-06-24; amended by O-21769 N.S., effective 2024-03-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies longer than 30 days (not fixed terms of 3 months or less) in residential rental property in San Diego.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, short-term occupancy, deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8), mobilehomes under MRL, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, dormitories, shared-facility rentals with live-in landlord, owner-occupied single-family residence, owner-occupied duplex, housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years, and separately alienable property (e.g. condos) whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member and tenants were given written notice.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive relief and damages including punitive; at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; at least 3x relocation assistance owed; attorney's fees; non-compliant notices void; City enforcement.
rules.interaction: Rights are in addition to state and federal rights; consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but gives greater relocation assistance.
rules.conflict_note: Local ordinance provides greater relocation assistance than Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 (1 month); treated as governing over the state rule where both apply.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property (condos) owned by non-corporate landlord with written notice
dormitories, care facilities, nonprofit transitional housing

rules.title: Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic software that analyzes nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels, and vendors may not sell or license it to landlords. Tenants can sue for injunctions, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus attorney's fees; each month and property is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 11
Prohibition of Anti-Competitive Automated Rent Price-Fixing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property
rules.effective_date_note: Official text (draft in D076) says effective on the 30th day after final passage with the date blank; June 2025 effective date taken from a law-firm alert (D002/D037).
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees.
rules.exemptions: Excludes software publishing reports from aggregated historical nonpublic data over 90 days old or public data without recommending future rents; software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits.
rules.conflict_note: Official source in corpus is the draft ordinance with blank passage date; enactment and June 2025 date rely on secondary sources.

unverifiable_exemptions: software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits

rules.title: San Diego source-of-income discrimination prohibition (unverified)
rules.requirement: San Diego appears to have a municipal division prohibiting discrimination based on a tenant's source of income, including housing vouchers. The text could not be read, so details are unverified.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 8
rules.quoted_span: Section 8 means residential rental property in which the tenant receives tenant-based housing assistance under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937, also known as the Housing Choice Voucher Program.
rules.conflict_note: Unverified: based only on link-only source D075 title (Division 8, prohibition of discrimination based on a tenant's source of income). Quoted span is from D073 and only generally relates to Section 8.

parsed.notes: Merged c64/c101 (just cause) and c65/c79/c92 (algorithmic). Rent caps, security deposits and application fees: no San Diego documents provided, so no records or findings. Source-of-income rule added as unverified from link-only D075.
